projects.title: Third-Person Soulslike Combat Prototype
projects.role: Gameplay & Combat Design / Blueprint Systems / Animation Retargeting
projects.summary: A third-person action prototype built entirely in Unreal Blueprint, focused on attack and dodge flow, hit feedback, projectile behavior, input response, and numerical tuning. Interfaces, Actor Components, and base classes are used to create an extensible modular structure.
projects.tools: Unreal Engine 5, Blueprint, Animation Montage, AnimNotifyState, Blueprint Interface, Actor Component, Data Asset

detail.overview: A third-person action prototype created entirely in Unreal Blueprint with no C++. The project tests attack, dodge, hit detection, and enemy feedback while also practicing maintainable system organization through EnemyBase, ProjectileBase, Actor Components, Blueprint Interfaces, and component tags to reduce direct casts and hard-coded references between modules.
whatIBuilt: Implemented light attacks, heavy attacks, dodge, stamina, lock-on, hit detection, damage, and enemy hit feedback.
Implemented projectile spawning, collision, valid-target checks, and cleanup.
Used AnimNotifyState to control active hit frames for different melee weapons and align impact feedback with UI damage numbers.
Handled input buffering and animation-state transitions to reduce sticky actions and state conflicts during fast combat.
Retargeted animation assets and connected animation, audio, VFX, and UI to combat events.
Used editable parameters, Data Assets, and visual Debug Traces to support rapid numerical iteration.

breakdown.label: Modular Communication
breakdown.text: Built reusable inheritance structures with EnemyBase and ProjectileBase, encapsulated part of the core logic in Actor Components, and used Blueprint Interfaces to reduce direct type dependencies. This lets different enemies and projectiles extend their own behavior while retaining shared logic.

breakdown.label: Animation Blueprint State Sync
breakdown.text: Obtained and cached the character reference during Animation Blueprint initialization to avoid repeated casts during every animation update. The cached Character Ref then reads movement, airborne, and combat states and synchronizes them to AnimBP variables that drive the state machine and combat animation transitions.

breakdown.label: Animation & Hit Logic
breakdown.text: Used AnimNotifyState to define the Combo Window during specific portions of attack animations. If the player presses the next attack during that window, the input is buffered and consumed when the current attack ends or transition conditions are met, improving responsiveness while preventing arbitrary attack switching and animation/state conflicts.

breakdown.label: Data-Driven Debugging
breakdown.text: Exposed damage multipliers, cooldowns, and hit windows as editable parameters, then used Draw Debug to calibrate attack range and invulnerability frames frame by frame.

challenges: Health logic is still managed directly by the character. A future iteration could separate it into an independent Health Component to improve reuse and reduce responsibilities in the character Blueprint.

After adding combos and input buffering, priority between attack state, animation state, and input state became more complex. Clear transition conditions and repeated testing are needed to avoid duplicate triggers or state conflicts.

Some early logic depended on direct casts and specific Actor references. As the system expanded, I gradually moved toward Base Classes and Blueprint Interfaces to reduce concrete type dependencies and make new enemies and projectiles easier to extend.
detail.workflowNotes: I repeatedly tested in PIE and used data-driven parameters plus visual debugging to quickly adjust damage multipliers, cooldowns, attack windows, and dodge invulnerability frames. AI tools supported research and troubleshooting; the final Blueprint structure, implementation, and validation were completed in Unreal Engine.

projects.title: Punk Plush Panic
projects.category: Unity · Capstone Project · 2.5D Platform Action · Team Project
projects.role: Combat Design / Level Design / VFX / Systems Design
projects.summary: A fast-paced 2.5D platform action game where players switch between three characters and combine abilities against enemy waves. I worked on combat and systems design, level iteration, VFX, and improving boss attack timing and readability.
projects.tools: Unity, Level Design, Boss Design, VFX, Playtest Feedback, Cross-Functional Collaboration

detail.overview: Punk Plush Panic was my capstone project, developed by a student team. Players switch between three characters and combine different abilities to handle enemy waves. My work focused on combat and systems design, level and encounter iteration, VFX feedback, organizing playtest feedback, and communicating with programmers to improve boss attack readability.
whatIBuilt: Contributed to gameplay mechanics, level encounters, and combat iteration, implementing and validating selected playable mechanics in Unity.
Designed and iterated level spaces, player routes, and encounter pacing, adjusting enemy pressure and character-switching opportunities based on playtests.

Late in development, proactively reduced parts of the level and non-core content based on the remaining schedule, focusing team resources on the core gameplay and helping the project reach a deliverable build on time.
Organized playtest feedback, converted readability, pacing, and level issues into specific action items, and pushed agreed changes forward with the team.
Adjusted boss skill timing when attack telegraphs were insufficient, then worked with programmers to add a pre-attack ground-range indicator that gave players a clearer reaction window.
Created smoke, environmental wind, early skill effects, Buff VFX, and other visual feedback. Some early effects were later replaced during the team's visual iteration.

breakdown.label: Boss Telegraphing & Reaction Window
breakdown.text: Adjusted boss skill timing and worked with programmers to add a ground-range indicator before attacks. Combining temporal and visual telegraphs improved readability and gave players a more reasonable reaction window.

breakdown.label: Configurable Portal Mechanic
breakdown.text: Implemented a configurable portal mechanic in Unity so level designers could quickly set entrances, exits, and trigger areas and reuse the mechanic across different scenes.

breakdown.label: Path-Driven Adjustable Level Trap
breakdown.text: Built a moving trap based on an editable path, allowing level designers to directly adjust its route, position, and behavior parameters. This reduced the need to repeatedly change underlying logic and improved level-testing efficiency.

breakdown.label: Player Capture-and-Release Trap | Cut Feature
breakdown.text: Prototyped an environmental trap that captures the player, temporarily restricts movement, and releases them after a short delay to create pacing variation and spatial danger. The mechanic reached a playable state but was later removed to control project scope.

breakdown.label: Level Scope Management & Delivery
breakdown.text: Based on the remaining schedule and core-gameplay priorities late in development, I proactively reduced parts of the level and non-core mechanics to focus team resources on deliverable content and help the project finish on time.

breakdown.label: Playtest Feedback & Iteration
breakdown.text: Used Google Docs to collect and organize playtest feedback, translated pacing, readability, and level issues into specific changes, and worked with the team to prioritize and implement actionable adjustments.

breakdown.label: VFX & Environmental Feedback
breakdown.text: Created smoke, environmental wind, early skill effects, Buff VFX, and other visuals to reinforce atmosphere and gameplay feedback. Some early effects were later replaced or removed based on the visual direction and project scope.

breakdown.label: Ability Design & Balance
breakdown.text: Used Excel to calculate player stats and designed three reaction types to support a smoother horde-clearing experience.

challenges: Early production showed me that level mechanics built around fixed paths and hard-coded parameters quickly become expensive to tune. I added editable paths and parameters to moving traps so level design could iterate directly in the scene without repeatedly changing underlying logic.

The capture-and-release trap and environmental wind reached playable prototype states, but they were still evaluated against schedule, core gameplay value, and production cost. This made me prioritize post-prototype decisions instead of keeping a feature simply because it had already been built.

Boss and level testing showed that numerical changes alone do not solve every experience problem. Attack timing, visual telegraphs, spatial positioning, and player expectations need to be considered together, so later iterations approached readability through numerical, visual, and level-design changes at the same time.
detail.workflowNotes: I first use playable prototypes and playtests to identify the problem, then decide whether the best response is a numerical, mechanical, visual-feedback, or level-structure change. In team projects, I also weigh remaining time and the core experience when deciding whether a feature is worth further investment.

projects.title: Breach Brew
projects.category: Commercial Project · Unreal Engine · Environmental Gameplay Systems
projects.role: Technical Design / Technical Art / Gameplay Systems Implementation
projects.summary: Designed and implemented an event-driven environmental temperature system in which hot and cold states dynamically affect gameplay logic, material parameters, and Niagara VFX, using visual feedback to improve the readability of environmental mechanics.
projects.tools: Unreal Engine, Blueprint, Material Parameters, Niagara, Environmental Interaction, Cross-Functional Collaboration

detail.overview: Breach Brew is a commercial game project. I contributed to the design and implementation of an environmental temperature system so temperature changes can drive gameplay states, material behavior, and Niagara effects, while collaborating with technical art and design teammates on in-engine integration.
whatIBuilt: Designed and implemented an event-driven temperature system in Blueprint.
Built gameplay-parameter-driven material controls for hot and cold transitions.
Connected Niagara VFX to temperature and environmental events to provide clear visual feedback.
Implemented interactive environmental mechanics and improved readability through gameplay testing.
Collaborated with technical art and design teammates to integrate gameplay systems and visual presentation.

breakdown.label: Parameterized Frost Material
breakdown.text: Used a unified parameter to control frost coverage in real time, allowing the amount of freezing to be adjusted and leaving an interface for later connection to temperature Gameplay data.

breakdown.label: Reusable Power Visual Component
breakdown.text: Used an Actor Component to drive device lighting and spark states from one reusable system that can be attached directly to different devices.

breakdown.label: Parameterized Niagara VFX
breakdown.text: Created airflow Niagara effects with real-time direction and intensity controls, plus spark feedback for damaged powered devices, all driven through Blueprint parameters.

breakdown.label: Foam Gun Prototype
breakdown.text: Implemented projectile impact, surface attachment, and foam-volume growth as a foundation for later breach-covering and sealing rules. Still in development.

challenges: Gameplay logic, materials, and VFX need to share a consistent data source so the visual state does not drift out of sync with the actual system state.
The visual direction needs to be established early; otherwise, many materials may need to be rebuilt later.
detail.workflowNotes: My workflow centers on rapid prototyping and parameterization: I first break gameplay requirements into controllable data, then implement them through Blueprint, Actor Components, materials, and Niagara while exposing key parameters for later tuning and reuse. Current implementations include a data-driven frost material, adjustable Spark / Wind Niagara, a reusable power Component, and a Bubble Gun prototype.

projects.title: The E Book
projects.category: 2026 · Commercial Project · Unity · Numerical Configuration & Data Tooling
projects.role: Numerical Configuration / Workflow Design / AI-Assisted Tool Development
projects.summary: Maintained complex gameplay-balancing Excel configurations and redesigned the spreadsheet structure and data workflow. Built an AI-assisted conversion tool that automatically transforms designer-friendly spreadsheets into Unity-readable data formats.
projects.tools: Excel, Unity, Basic Python, AI-Assisted Development, Data Validation

detail.overview: On The E Book, I maintained gameplay numerical configurations and restructured the Excel workflow when designers found data editing cumbersome. I then used an AI-assisted workflow to develop a conversion tool that automatically turns designer-facing Excel data into configuration files Unity can read directly.
whatIBuilt: Created and maintained complex gameplay-balancing Excel configuration sheets.
Redesigned spreadsheet structures so designers could understand, fill in, and batch-adjust data more easily.
Used an AI-assisted workflow to develop an automatic Excel-to-Unity configuration conversion tool.
Reduced time spent on manual cleanup, copying, and format conversion, while lowering data-entry errors.
Worked with designers to verify that the new workflow supported real numerical iteration needs.

breakdown.label: Designer-Friendly Input
breakdown.text: Let designers maintain numerical data in readable spreadsheets instead of directly editing engine-facing formats, including difficulty-curve control, item creation, enemy creation, and previewing stat changes after equipping items.

breakdown.label: Automatic Conversion
breakdown.text: Converted Excel data into Unity-readable configuration formats to reduce repetitive manual work.

breakdown.label: Error Control
breakdown.text: Used structural constraints and validation to reduce missing fields, formatting errors, and version mismatches.

breakdown.label: Iteration Efficiency
breakdown.text: Shortened the path between a data change and in-engine validation to support faster numerical testing.

challenges: The spreadsheet needed to remain easy for designers to read while still being structured strictly enough for reliable tool conversion.
Public portfolio material needs to hide commercially sensitive data and show only sanitized table structures, tool flows, and sample output.
detail.workflowNotes: For a public portfolio presentation, use fictional or sanitized data to show before-and-after comparisons: the original spreadsheet, the restructured version, the conversion button or logs, and the successful result loaded in Unity.

whatIBuilt: Implemented selected puzzle interactions and door-state logic.
Adjusted interaction distance, feedback, and handling based on the VR control experience.
Completed parts of the level and environment assembly.
Created and tuned glass, water, and other environmental materials.

breakdown.label: Puzzle Logic
breakdown.text: Connected puzzle conditions, interaction results, and scene states into testable flows.

breakdown.label: Door & State Logic
breakdown.text: Handled door conditions, open/closed states, and interaction feedback.

breakdown.label: VR Interaction Feel
breakdown.text: Adjusted interaction range, feedback speed, and object handling based on the actual headset experience.

breakdown.label: Environment & Materials
breakdown.text: Used environment assembly plus glass, water, and other materials to strengthen spatial readability and immersion.

challenges: Distances and feedback that seem reasonable on a desktop can feel sluggish or unnatural in a headset, so interaction tuning needs to be tested in VR.
detail.workflowNotes: This project is best demonstrated with a short video of puzzle and door logic, supported by screenshots of materials and environment assembly. There is no need to split every small mechanic into a separate project.
